whatsHappening.background: Since independence in 1960, the Central African Republic has faced repeated coups, weak state control and chronic insecurity. The current crisis grew out of years of failed peace efforts, then escalated sharply in 2013 when Seleka rebels captured Bangui and anti-Balaka militias formed in response. Although elections and peace agreements followed, armed groups kept operating across much of the country outside Bangui. Violence, displacement and weak public services still shape everyday life for civilians.

Seleka captures Bangui, Bozize is removed, and anti-Balaka militias soon emerge.
The UN creates MINUSCA to protect civilians and help stabilize the country.
The government and 14 armed groups sign a peace deal, but most of it is not implemented.
The CPC threatens Bangui before government forces push back with support from MINUSCA, Rwanda and Wagner fighters.

civilianImpact.experiences: Civilians in the Central African Republic have lived through years of armed violence, forced displacement, disrupted schooling, weak public services and severe poverty. Humanitarian needs remain high, especially for children. Many communities still struggle to access clean water, education, health care and safety, while recurring violence keeps forcing families from their homes.

whatsHappening.background: The conflict in the Central African Republic is not only a military crisis. It is also a humanitarian crisis shaped by displacement, poverty, disrupted education and weak access to water and basic services. Children and families in remote areas are often the most affected, and insecurity can also block aid from reaching them.

civilianImpact.experiences: For many civilians, the crisis means much more than headline fighting. It means children missing school, families lacking clean water, communities living with displacement and daily life shaped by fear and economic hardship. Long-running conflict has weakened already fragile systems and left many people dependent on humanitarian support.

whatsHappening.background: Support is most effective when it goes to organizations already working in the Central African Republic and when it helps raise awareness about a crisis that is often overlooked. Even simple public attention matters because underreported crises often struggle to attract enough sustained aid.

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping the Central African Republic means responding to a crisis that is both severe and underreported. Donations can support children, displaced families, education, water access and protection services, while awareness helps keep the crisis from being ignored.
